The Delhi High Court on Tuesday refused to stay the investigation in a case filed against a woman journalist for making alleged casteist remarks against a police officer during a protest near Jantar Mantar earlier this month.
Justice Mini Pushkarna said the court was not rejecting the interim prayer at this stage and it was also not passing any order on it.
The court issued notice to Delhi Police and Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat, the complainant in the case, on the journalist’s petition seeking quashing of the FIR, and asked them to file their replies before November 16, the next date of hearing.
“I am simply issuing notice on the petition and the interim application. Unless and until I have their (police) stand, I can’t stay the investigation. I will hear it on merits once I have their reply. The investigation will continue,” the judge said.
“I am not rejecting any prayer as of now. I am only issuing notice to them. The matter needs consideration; list for final hearing on November 16,” the judge added.
The high court also passed a similar order on another plea by a male colleague of the woman journalist seeking quashing of the FIR registered against him.
Earlier, the woman journalist had filed a sexual assault complaint against ACP Bhagat. Her complaint is being investigated by the Delhi Police Crime Branch.
During the hearing on Tuesday, the scribe’s counsel contended that the FIR filed by the ACP was lodged only to intimidate her into not pursuing the complaint against him.
He submitted that the woman journalist herself belonged to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) community of Nagaland.
The counsel further contended that the woman went to the police station on October 3 to lodge an FIR, but police registered the case 10 days later on October 13.
However, ACP Bhagat gave his complaint on October 13 and the FIR was lodged within minutes, he said.
Delhi Police registered the FIR against the independent journalist and others on a complaint by Mr. Bhagat, posted at the Connaught Place sub-division of New Delhi district, alleging casteist remarks, public humiliation and defamation directed at the officer during the protest.
